geometry_edits.rationale: Deepen the threshold notch so the ground response becomes more legible as an occupiable public seam.
Widen the notch to strengthen publicness and reduce the sense of a sealed frontage.
Match the carved ground response to the site access side indicated in the program frame.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the carved void to the verified access side so the ground response reads as an entry threshold rather than a generic subtraction.
Broaden the cavity to strengthen publicness and make the access seam legible in plan and elevation.
Increase void depth so the subtraction becomes a real ground condition instead of a shallow nick.
Reduce the bend slightly to keep the dominant gesture but calm the silhouette and improve section clarity for neighborhood living.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant bent bar, so the core gesture is legible and the form is not overly fragmented. However, across the four views the mass behaves more like a sloped, compressed object than a clearly active neighborhood-building. The blue access edge is not answered by a convincing public threshold; the notch/cave is too weak and semantically muted to read as a public court, entry seam, or ground-floor openness. Sectionally, the object trends toward a long tilted mass with a chopped end rather than a program-supporting ground/public sequence with calm upper hierarchy. It is visually coherent, but not yet coherent in the program sense required for neighborhood living.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise pavilion massing with a carved central void and a clear bridge/threshold condition can support neighborhood-scale public program.
Interlocking rectilinear volumes with a large courtyard and elevated connections suggest a strong public interior/exterior sequence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More singular and simpler than the candidate; limited continuity and weaker void logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact pavilion with a small vertical element and a simple entry canopy can inform a neighborhood-edge street building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual housing typology; useful only for terrace/courtyard transfer, not as a program model.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard residential section can inform stepped massing and communal voids, but the housing typology is not the target program.

warnings: Visible mass is coherent but underdeveloped as a public-ground building.
Access edge response is too weak relative to the verified frontage.
Section reads as an abstract bent object more than an active mixed-use threshold.
No serious view-to-view collision issue, but the form is close to a single-view idea rather than a fully resolved massing system.
